Subject: Next steps: technical deep-dive & dedicated sizing for Finova

Hi Sofia —

Great meeting this morning, thanks for taking the time. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we keep momentum: 

- Recap: Finova is evaluating Redwood Dedicated for high-throughput inference for your document-to-entity pipeline. Key success criteria: sub-150ms p95 response for 512-token prompts, sustained concurrency up to ~120 qps during peak batch windows, and predictable cost for forecasting.
- Immediate next step: technical deep-dive + dedicated capacity sizing call to align on traffic shape, token-level economics, and a mutual action plan.

Proposed slots (PST):
  * Thu Dec 7 — 09:00–10:00 (PST) — technical deep-dive + runbook review
  * Fri Dec 8 — 16:00–17:00 (PST) — dedicated sizing + throughput profiling

If neither works I can share 2 more options. For the sizing call we’ll need a few artifacts beforehand so we can come prepared:
  1) Representative request payloads (sample documents and typical prompt templates)
  2) Expected tokens per request and average/peak concurrency by hour
  3) Any latency SLOs (p50/p95/p99 targets) and burst patterns (e.g., 30min batch windows)

I’ve attached a short discovery notes PDF and a mutual action plan spreadsheet to this thread — please review and add any missing items.

Thanks — I’ll hold the two slots tentatively and will finalize based on your pick.

— Markus
Markus Klein
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments: Discovery-notes-Finova.pdf (summary), MAP-Finova.xlsx (mutual action plan)
From: Sofia Gomes <sofia.gomes@finova.com>

Date: 2028-12-05T14:04:00+00:00
Subject: Re: Next steps: technical deep-dive & dedicated sizing for Finova

Markus —

Thanks for the clear recap. Appreciate the two options — Fri Dec 8 16:00 PST works best for our engineering leads. I’ll include Henry Lo (platform lead) on the call.

A couple of quick notes from our side before the sizing call:
- We will send two sample payloads: one short (customer chat summarization, ~200 tokens) and one long (multi-page document parse, ~1,800 tokens).
- Our expected baseline concurrency is ~40 qps with two 20-minute burst windows in the morning and late afternoon where we expect up to 120 qps for ~30 minutes.
- Latency target: p95 < 200ms for the short payload; we understand the long payload will vary but aim for p95 < 500ms.

Can you share a pre-call checklist or a short template for the payloads so we send exactly what you need? Also please send the calendar invite to Dec 8 16:00 PST.

Best,
Sofia Gomes
Director, Platform Engineering — Finova
sofia.gomes@finova.com

Hi Sofia — looping in our Solutions Engineering lead for the sizing call: Evelyn Hart (evelyn.hart@redwood.ai). We’ll own the pre-call checklist; attaching a short CSV template to make it easy to populate.

Pre-call items (what we need 24–48 hours before the Dec 8 call):
- 2 sample payloads (raw and tokenized if possible) — short and long
- Expected tokens/request (avg and 95th) and a sample distribution by hour/day
- Typical request concurrency and anticipated burst length + frequency
- Any authentication or VPC/firewall constraints we should plan for

If you can paste an example prompt that will be used in production, that helps us calibrate batching/kv cache behavior. For capacity estimation we’ll also ask for a rough monthly token volume estimate so we can produce cost trade-offs between Dedicated and hosting variants.

I’ve attached: Sizing-template.csv (simple columns for payload name, tokens_estimate, avg_qps, peak_qps, comments).

Thanks — we’ll follow up with a calendar invite for Dec 8 16:00 PST and a short agenda.

— Grace
Grace O'Connor
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference

Attachments: Sizing-template.csv
